name: Ysra Tal
appearance: Slight and very upright, her hair cropped short as a page's and a thin old scar running up from her right brow, in a dark coat cut close for riding with six dark buttons down its front and gloves of thin dark leather that fit like skin. She sits a long-legged horse without shifting, keeps her hands quiet, and moves on ice as if it had been laid down for her.
portrait_alt: Portrait of Ysra Tal: a slight woman with black hair cropped short as a page's, a fine-boned face, level dark eyes and a thin old scar running up from her right brow, in a dark high-collared riding coat with dark buttons down its front, one hand in a glove of thin dark leather at her collar, before a snowy stone weir, a frozen river and a mill's wheel.
last_seen_doing: Came up the river in the night after the lamps with four riders, sat her horse on the west bank of the Wend, inclined her head to him once and did not follow onto the ice.
now: On the west bank of the Wend by the marsh with four riders, watching.
story_so_far: Sent from Calden to bring in the captain of the Ninth alive and not told why, Ysra Tal lost a day to the carter's lying road, watched the company from a distance, and summoned him under the forms to the weir. Her one question was why he would not kneel. At the noon bell her footwork found a man who would not move, and she went down on the ice with his point in her shoulder, wanting a reason for the first time.

quote.text: That is what I will call you when I tell him.

known_facts.fact: She told Darrow she has orders to bring him in alive and was not told why, and that she will take him at the mill's noon bell whether he has answered her or not.
known_facts.evidence: I have orders to bring you in alive, Captain. I was not told why.

known_facts.fact: She came from Calden on an order to bring in the captain of the Ninth Lance alive, with no reason given.
known_facts.evidence: She had read it twice, which was once more than an order needed

known_facts.fact: In Calden they call her the Needle.
known_facts.evidence: In Calden they called her the Needle.

known_facts.fact: She read the carter's two carts out of one at the spring, believed it, and lost a day to the wrong lane.
She keeps a small book for the things she has been wrong about.
known_facts.evidence: She kept a small book for the things she had been wrong about.

known_facts.fact: She had never met a man who would not move.
known_facts.evidence: She had never in her life met one who would not.

known_facts.fact: She found she wanted to know why she had been sent for him alive.
known_facts.evidence: She found that she wanted to know why she had been sent for him alive.

known_facts.fact: She took a wound in the left shoulder from a man who did not move, and was astonished by it.
known_facts.evidence: a wound from a man who had not moved

known_facts.fact: She was told, when given him, that the captain of the Ninth took his Lance into the Wend on a morning when everyone knew the Grace would be thin, and that the Second was told to hold the west bank.
known_facts.evidence: That the Second was told to hold the west bank, and held it.

known_facts.fact: She did not know what she had told him.
known_facts.evidence: She had no idea what she had said.

known_facts.fact: She noticed that his message left out what she had told him on the ice.
known_facts.evidence: You left out what I told you

known_facts.fact: She said she would call him Plainspoken when she told the man who sent her: he said exactly what he meant, and not one word over.
known_facts.evidence: You said exactly what you meant, and not one word over.

known_facts.fact: From the top of the far bank she looked back once at the girl with the ledger, the way a clerk fixes a page in her head.
known_facts.evidence: the way a clerk looks at a page to fix it in her head

known_facts.fact: She watched him cross the Wend from the west bank and did not come onto the ice.

relationships.label: sent to bring him in alive
relationships.note: Summoned him under the forms to the weir below the mill, asked why he will not kneel, and found a man who would not move.
